content.title: About
content.content: The Meatloaf sandwich is a sandwich that uses a classic meatloaf—made from ground beef, pork or a blend, mixed with onion, breadcrumbs and spices—as the filling. The loaf is baked, sliced thinly, and placed between two slices of bread, often with cheese, lettuce, tomato and a sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Meatloaf originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a way to stretch leftover meat.
Traditional recipes often add tomato sauce or ketchup to the meat mixture for moisture.
Meatloaf sandwiches are a staple in school cafeterias and quick‑service eateries because they are fast and filling.
Variations may include cheddar cheese, bacon, or pickles for extra flavor.
In some regions the loaf is baked in a “house” shape and then sliced into sandwich‑size portions.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Meatloaf provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef and pork in the loaf supply iron, which is important for blood formation.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B12, B6 and niacin support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Fiber from bread
items.content: Using whole‑grain bread adds dietary fiber to the sandwich.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of protein, fat and carbs provides lasting satiety.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Meat and cheese can raise saturated fat intake, which may be a concern for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt added to the meat mixture and sauces can contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper cooking or storage of meatloaf can lead to salmonella or other bacterial contamination.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: If wheat bread is used, people with celiac disease need a gluten‑free alternative.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is usually served warm so the meatloaf stays tender. Add lettuce, tomato slices, pickles, mustard or mayo for extra flavor. For a lighter option choose whole‑grain or rye bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Meatloaf itself can be frozen for up to 3 months; reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
